deepdive.sec: Auto Components / Wheels & Chassis Systems (steel + aluminium)

bull_bear.body: Heavy growth-capex phase (~Rs 600 cr) funded on a levered balance sheet: borrowings ~Rs 826 cr (8–9%) + Rs 400–500 cr factoring limits (used for working-capital spikes, e.g. the Rs 150 cr aluminium RM surge). An analyst explicitly suggested an equity raise to "lighten the balance sheet" for minority shareholders — management noted without commitment. No buyback/dividend detail. Capital is going almost entirely into aluminium (wheels + knuckles) and steel agri/PV capacity where SSWL "strongly dominates."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Balance-sheet leverage:** Rs 826 cr debt + Rs 400–500 cr factoring during a Rs 600 cr capex year; working-capital swings on volatile aluminium prices; equity-raise suggestion unanswered.
- **Domestic alloy margin war:** competitors pricing "below cost" — SSWL insulated via exports/premium but domestic alloy margins "crashing."
- **Commissioning concentration:** Bhuj trial + agri brownfield both target Q4 FY27 — execution/slippage risk.
- **West Asia war + commodity volatility:** repeatedly flagged; aluminium price swings (mitigated by monthly pass-through).
- **Tariff / export dependence:** stabilized at 10% level field but "not fully gone away"; export recovery thesis hinges on it holding.
- **EV-program uncertainty:** knuckles seeded on Mahindra's EV program — EV-market "ups and downs" a swing factor (mitigated by second customer + new awards).
- **Truck-segment softness:** monsoon-linked "blip"; management expects post-monsoon buoyancy.
- **China/Arays dependence:** Bhuj aftermarket capability leans on Chinese technical partner Arays.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, promotional, and unusually candid on the "bull run I've never seen in 30–40 years." MD Dheeraj Garg is emphatic on his framework (EBITDA/wheel over EBITDA-%, absolute over percentage) and pushed back firmly on an analyst's "steel is a laggard" premise. He was self-aware about conservatism ("I was being conservative… it exceeded my expectations") and disciplined on not over-guiding ("I don't want to jump the gun… next quarter I'll talk again"). Notably transparent about competitive dynamics (only 2 alloy players, below-cost competition) yet guarded on proprietary detail (steel-vs-alloy EBITDA split deferred to next call; Bhuj/Arays specifics withheld from competitors). Tone: bullish, execution-confident, shareholder-aware (acknowledged the equity-raise suggestion).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The margin jump is pricing, not just mix:** management is explicit that EBITDA/wheel Rs 262 → Rs 314 is mostly two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1–5%, more pending) — a durable, contracted step-up, not a cyclical mix fluke.
- **Steel wheels flipped from structural decliner to growth engine** post-GST-cuts — a genuine narrative reversal (industry "sold out of capacity," 15–20 years of pass-car-steel problems "come to an end") that justifies the Rs 150 cr agri/PV brownfield.
- **Track absolute EBITDA + EBITDA/wheel, ignore EBITDA-%** — the single most repeated instruction; RM-price volatility makes the percentage actively misleading (higher RM can mean more money at a lower %).
- **Aluminium is de-risked to a pure pass-through** — the shift to monthly settlement makes SSWL "back-to-back neutral," so aluminium-price headlines should not scare on margins.
- **Capacity, not demand, is the binding constraint** — knuckles at 100%, all units >95%, Bhuj "sold out" pre-commissioning; the investable question is execution/commissioning timing (Q4 FY27), not order intake.
- **Export-over-domestic is the real long-game** — SSWL wants exports > domestic within 10 years, using India's low-cost base; domestic alloy price war is being sidestepped, not fought.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Consistent Dividend paid by the Company": the dividend-declared series runs from FY13 to FY26 and ends at 150%, with a 0% year marked "^Covid Year" (FY20); face value per share was "upto FY21 – Rs 10, from FY22 – Rs 5, from FY23 – Rs 1".
- Balance-sheet KPIs slide plots two five-year series for FY22-FY26 — 374 / 222 / 487 / 371 / 382 and 282 / 274 / 310 / 311 / 331 — labelled "Long Term Debt (Rs. in Crs.)" and "Cash Accruals (Rs. in Crs.)"; the extraction does not make clear which series carries which label.
- Leverage ratios (FY22→FY26): Debt/EBITDA 1.55, 1.31, 2.11, 1.65, 1.57 and Debt/Equity 0.76, 0.52, 0.79, 0.55, 0.49 as printed; Current Ratio 1.00, 0.97, 1.01, 1.03, 1.09 and Fixed Asset Turnover 2.6, 3.0, 3.0, 2.7, 2.8.
- Return profile as on 31st March 2026: "RoCE* 18.0%", "RoE* 12.0%" and "Cash & Cash Equivalents* Rs. 6.5 Crs." (deck definitions: "RoCE = EBIT / (Total Assets – Current Liabilities), RoE = PAT / Total Equity (Excl Capital Reserve)").
- Cash Conversion Cycle (in Days, Mar-22→Mar-26) shown as 56, 48, 57, 50, 51 with component series Inventory / Debtors / Creditors of 106, 100, 89, 94, 100; 33, 25, 30, 32, 36; and 84, 77, 62, 77, 86 as printed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Alloy (aluminium) wheels — 35%:** strongest growth driver; domestic leadership; only ~2 serious players; SSWL commands a price premium in select cases as the "technically superior" producer. Domestic alloy margins "crashing" (competitors pricing below cost) — SSWL's answer is export diversification, not a price war ("we are not in the cash-burning business").
- **Aluminium knuckles — 2%:** Rs ~23 cr this quarter; running at 100% utilization; 2 customers (started with Mahindra EV program, added a second); FY27 revenue guided Rs 110–130 cr (doubling); export traction expected in 12–18 months.
- **Truck + Tractor — 34%:** tractor strong (rural recovery, higher-HP mechanization, GST-cut affordability); truck a small "blip" last month (monsoon) but structural CV boom intact (replacement + infra + freight).
- **Steel wheels (the reversal):** long-called a "declining business," now growing post-GST-cuts; pass-car steel guided >5% growth; industry "sold out of capacity" — driving the Rs 150 cr agri/PV steel brownfield.
- **Exports:** diversified across Europe/Latin America; tariff drag stabilized (10%, level playing field vs Vietnam/Thailand); June +7% YoY.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Lowest-cost producer ex-China:** MD asserts "80–90% true… ex-China, hands down, lowest-cost producer" — the structural edge letting SSWL win exports on a level tariff field and refuse below-cost domestic pricing.
- **Aluminium-wheel duopoly + technical premium:** only ~2 serious players; SSWL's technical superiority earns a price premium in select cases and insulates margins as it pivots volume to exports.
- **Back-to-back aluminium pass-through:** moved from quarterly to **monthly** settlement during the West Asia crisis — 30-day lag matched to supplier lag, making SSWL "fully insulated on both downside and upside" of aluminium prices (a hard-won contractual moat vs the prior regime where it "would have lost millions of crores").
- **OEM input-price increases secured:** two years of pushing yielded 1–5% increases (more pending) — pricing power evidenced, not asserted.

business.body:
- "SSWL is a leader in designing & manufacturing Automotive wheels – both Steel & Alloy Wheels category" and "aspires to be the Preferred Global Brand of Wheel Solution provider committed to excellence"; founded in 1991.
- Strategic shareholder alliances: Tata Steel Limited (Strategic Alliance Agreement of January 2008, 6.9% stake) supports "flexibility in areas such as supply chain management, enjoying priorities and stronger support for new grade developments"; Nippon Steel Corporation / Sumitomo Metal Industries (Strategic Alliance Agreement of December 2010, 5.4% stake) "helps in bringing international expertise in steel quality and newer technology exploration". The deck footnotes the stakes as "% Stake is as of 31 st June 2026".
- Deep OEM entrenchment with high share-of-business at named customers, e.g. in the alloy-wheel key-customer slide: Hyundai 74% (Creta, Creta EV, Alcazar, Venue, New Venue, Verna, Grand i10, Aura, Exter), Mahindra 64% (3XO, Bolero Neo, Scorpio Classic, Thar Roxx, XUV 700, Scorpio N, XeV 9s, Be6), TATA Motors 62% (Harrier, Altroz, Nexon, Punch, Sierra), Renault 60% (Duster, Kiger), Kia 51% (Carens EV, Carens, Seltos, Sonnet, Syros, Syros EV), Skoda 47% (Slavia, Kylaq), MG 25% (Hector, Astor), Nissan 20% (Magnite).
- Steel-wheel customer share-of-business examples: JCB 62%, Escorts 60%, Mahindra 56%, Sonalika 48%, New Holland 31%; Ashok Leyland 64% and TATA Motors 58%; HMSI 39%, Suzuki Scooters 96%, Mahindra 3W 81%; Maruti Suzuki 36%, Hyundai 25%, Honda 96%, MG Motors 100%, Kia 30%.
- Broad export footprint: customer locations listed across Brazil, Japan, Poland, Thailand, Romania, Russia, Italy, Morocco, Slovakia, Germany, France, UK, Colombia, Argentina, Netherlands, S Korea, Canada, U.A.E., Egypt, Spain, Austria, Hungary, USA and Australia.
- Stated 6 Year CAGR: "Revenue ~20%, PAT ~27%".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] "Acquisition of AMW Autocomponent Limited at Bhuj, Gujarat" in 2024, taken "through NCLT order", is now the site for the aluminium wheels and knuckles capacity expansion.
- [Exports / tariffs] "While the reported numbers are domestic-demand led, exports began showing signs of recovery in June as tariff-related disruptions normalized — a potential tailwind for coming quarters."
- [Reporting basis] All financial statements, the Q1 FY27 snapshot and the historical P&L, balance sheet and cash flow in this deck are explicitly "On Standalone Basis".
- [Milestone history] Journey markers include first steel wheel commercial production at Dappar, Punjab (1991), 2W & tractor wheels (2002), LCV wheels (2006), start of exports to PSA Peugeot Citroen, France and HCV wheels (2007), Chennai plant (2008), semi-fullface styled wheel for Renault Romania (2009), Jamshedpur plant (2010), truck wheels at Chennai and PV alloy wheels at Mehsana with 1.5 Mn capacity (2017).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Margin expansion (+40 bps, EBITDA/wheel Rs 262 → Rs 314) is driven by: (1) OEM input-price increases ex-RM (the single biggest lever, ">1% on margins," more to flow); (2) operating leverage at >95% utilization; (3) premium/alloy mix; (4) cost optimization + AI-led labour productivity. Management insists on **EBITDA/wheel over EBITDA-%** because volatile RM prices (aluminium +Rs 150 cr this quarter) distort the ratio. Aluminium is a genuine pass-through (monthly settlement, back-to-back neutral). Manpower issues of the prior year "fully resolved." PAT margin 4.7%, guided toward 6% on volume + margin.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue Rs 1,509 cr (+27%); EBITDA Rs 165.17 cr (+32%, +40 bps); EBITDA/wheel Rs 314 (vs Rs 262); PAT Rs 71.51 cr (+43%, 4.7% margin). Mix: alloy 35%, truck+tractor 34%, knuckles 2%, VA ~70%. Exports Rs 127 cr (+37% QoQ; June +7% YoY, first rise in 2 yrs). All plants >95% util; knuckles 100% (sold out). Debt ~Rs 826 cr + factoring Rs 400–500 cr; aluminium RM +Rs 150 cr (passed on). Guidance: FY27 rev 20%+ (~Rs 6,500 cr), EBITDA ~Rs 650 cr, EBITDA/wheel >Rs 310–315, exports ~Rs 600 cr, knuckles Rs 110–130 cr (2x). Capex ~Rs 600 cr: Bhuj (alloy 1.2 mn + knuckles 1.1 mn, trial Q4 FY27, →6.2 mn alu wheels) + agri/PV steel brownfield Rs 150 cr (24→26 mn, commercialize by CY2026-end). New-capacity ≥80% util by Q1 FY28.
- _Next Q → check: EBITDA/wheel vs Rs 314 (upside-bias promise); export ramp toward Rs 600 cr + tariff stability; Bhuj trial production (Q4) + agri brownfield commissioning slippage; knuckles revenue doubling toward Rs 110–130 cr; PAT-margin move toward 6%; any equity raise on the Rs 826 cr debt; steel-vs-alloy EBITDA split disclosure (promised)._

outlook.body:
- **Top-line growth:** **20%+** FY27; target ~**Rs 6,500 cr** (~25% on run-rate).
- **EBITDA/wheel:** from Rs 262 (FY26) to **>Rs 310–315** through FY27; **upside bias on Rs 314** (review after Q2).
- **Absolute EBITDA:** ~**Rs 650 cr** FY27 (on ~Rs 6,500 cr revenue).
- **Exports:** ~**Rs 600 cr** FY27; then aim **20%+ growth** thereafter (long-run: exports > domestic within 10 years).
- **Knuckles revenue:** **Rs 110–130 cr** FY27 — roughly **doubling** YoY.
- **Alloy mix:** ~**35–37%** of revenue.
- **Bhuj plants:** alloy wheel 1.2 mn/yr + knuckles 1.1 mn/yr → aluminium segment ~**6.2 mn wheels**; **trial production Q4 FY27**.
- **Agri/PV steel brownfield:** ~**Rs 150 cr**, steel capacity **24 mn → 26 mn**, commercialize **before end of CY2026** (Q4 FY27).
- **Total FY27 capex:** ~**Rs 600 cr** (Bhuj Rs 420 cr + replacement Rs 80 cr + agri brownfield Rs 150 cr, split over FY27/FY28).
- **New-capacity utilization:** ≥**80% by Q1 FY28** (knuckles earlier).
- **PAT margin:** trajectory toward **6%** (from 4.7%) via volume + margin.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not a classic order-book business, but demand visibility is exceptional: **all business units >95% utilization**; knuckles at **100%** with the Bhuj order book "almost completely sold out" before commissioning. Export OEM awards (non-US geographies — Europe, Latin America) ramping over the next 3 quarters. New-customer nominations continuing. Management describes a "structural boom" in CV (3–5 yr run) and tractor/agri (10–15 yr, GST-cut driven) — capacity, not demand, is the constraint.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Bhuj aluminium complex** (alloy 1.2 mn + knuckles 1.1 mn) with technical partner **Arays** — aftermarket + OEM, predominantly **export-facing**; a global-player ambition ("dominant player of aluminium wheels in the world").
- **Aluminium knuckles into exports** — OEMs already know SSWL's capability from alloy wheels; 12–18-month ramp.
- **Hot stamping** — under discussion for existing OEM relationships (chassis/body lightweighting adjacency).
- **Agri-wheel brownfield** — fungible line (agri + passenger-car steel), +up to 2 mn wheels, hedged growth.
- **Export > domestic** — explicit 10-year strategic goal.
